question: Can the identifiability probe (diagnose_observability.py) serve as a per-cell deployment statistic that orders expert rungs by realized value?
design: Two ladder extremes (transformer 1-layer 'small', anchor MSE .3721; transformer 3-layer 'large', anchor MSE .3562), METR-LA, seed 101, three targets (0, 58, 147), 2000 train / 1200 test episodes, ridge-only probes, 5-fold style held-out evaluation as implemented.
hypothesis_under_test: Realized share should track the probe's out-of-sample R^2 for the marginal (refinement of Corollary 1: residual predictability governs realizable value).
findings: Probe R^2 is statistically indistinguishable from zero for BOTH extremes: state-only mean -0.004 (sd 0.019) for the weak rung and -0.015 (sd 0.028) for the strong rung, over three targets with 1200 test episodes each.

The probe's value statistic must be read against the per-cell random baseline, which varies from 0.115 to 0.294 of the oracle across these six cells. Excess over random is +0.048 (weak rung) and +0.067 (strong rung) in units of oracle, with per-cell spread of 0.09.

The ladder's own effect on the same two rungs is 0.268 vs 0.063 realized share, a 0.205 gap in the same units. The probe's excess is roughly a quarter of the effect it is supposed to explain and an order of magnitude noisier relative to its size.
The probe's ordering is therefore not merely noisy but uninformative: it cannot resolve an effect the ladder protocol resolves with paired confidence intervals on eight targets.

Consequence: the proposed deployment rule 'if probe R^2 < tau then fall back to the whole pool' is UNSUPPORTED and is not shipped. All probe R^2 in this study lie below any usable tau, so the rule would degenerate to always falling back.

also_recorded.anchor_mse_orders_rungs_within_a_family: Within the four neural rungs anchor MSE orders realized share perfectly (Spearman +1.0): higher anchor error, more realizable value, as Corollary 1 predicts. The relation breaks when the ridge rung is included (ridge has the worst anchor MSE .3782 but a share of .198, below the weak neural rung's .268).
also_recorded.slope: Fitted within the neural family the slope is 10.5 realized-share points per unit anchor MSE, i.e. a 1% anchor-MSE change (0.0036) corresponds to about +0.038 realized share. Over all five rungs the slope halves to 4.9 and monotonicity fails.
also_recorded.interpretation: The residual magnitude is a sufficient statistic for realizable value only within a fixed hypothesis class. Across classes the inductive bias changes which candidates are jointly improvable, so anchor error and residual geometry decouple. This is the cross-family exception already noted in the ladder discussion, now quantified.
